successors.note: The page: 'the city became an arrondissement in the newly created Département de la Roer' in 1798; 'The French occupation ended in 1814, when Cologne was occupied by Prussian and Russian troops'; in 1815 Cologne and the Rhineland were allocated to Prussia.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Cologne city row). The page gives no territory for the city-state ('Area ... not on page'; the only figure is 96.8 ha for the Roman colonia). A 12 km circle at Cologne (6.96E 50.94N, the circle electorate-of-cologne uses for the 1288 loss) is a soft stand-in; Deutz is named as a part of Cologne without a date.

ledger.note: 5 June 1288: Worringen. 'The Battle of Worringen was fought on 5 June 1288'; Archbishop Siegfried 'was taken prisoner by John of Brabant'; 'the City of Cologne gained its independence from the Archbishopric'. The Cologne page: 'after the Battle of Worringen in 1288' the city gained almost complete freedom from its archbishop.
1475: a free imperial city. 'In 1475 it was formally made a free imperial city, a status that it held until annexed by France on May 28, 1796.'
1794: the French. 'The French Revolutionary Wars resulted in the occupation of Cologne and the Rhineland in 1794.' The page gives no day.

region.text: the city of Cologne under French occupation

ledger.note: 28 May 1796: annexation. The occupation ends in annexation (the dissolve event below).

28 May 1796: annexed by France. 'A status that it held until annexed by France on May 28, 1796'; in 1798 the city became an arrondissement in the Département de la Roer, and in 1801 all its citizens were granted French citizenship.

certainty.note: The page gives no territory for the city-state; the circle is a stand-in and the extramural lands are not known.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (the Cologne article, which the site serves under 'Free Imperial City of Cologne', plus the Worringen page already opened for electorate-of-cologne; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Cologne city row.

SCOPE. 5 June 1288 (independence of the city after Worringen; the Cologne page: 'after the Battle of Worringen in 1288') to the annexation by France on 28 May 1796 (the page's sentence; the Cologne dossier of this batch, electorate-of-cologne, has the archbishop's lands French from 1794 and annexed in 1801 by Lunéville). The page's 1475 formal status date is a rename. The Cologne War (1583-1588) and the Thirty Years' War are mentioned without dates; no war entries. The page is the article on the city of Cologne in general (100,000 characters, read to the 100,000th character), so no territory beyond the city and Deutz is known.
